_note: Original questions for cycliq. Every answer is something stated in data/library.json, so a quiz never teaches a fact the library does not. `answer` is the index into `options`.

daily.q: What counts as day 1 of your cycle?
daily.explain: A cycle is counted from the first day of bleeding to the day before the next bleed starts.

daily.q: In a well-known study, about what share of people with 28-day cycles actually ovulated on day 14?
daily.explain: Only about 14% did. The most common ovulation day was day 16, and the range ran from day 11 to day 20. That is why cycliq predicts a window, not a day.

daily.q: A sustained rise in basal body temperature tells you what?
daily.explain: Progesterone raises temperature after the egg is released, so BBT confirms ovulation after the fact. It does not predict it.

daily.q: Which part of the cycle tends to stay the most consistent for one person?
daily.explain: The luteal phase usually holds at roughly ten to sixteen days. The follicular phase absorbs most of the variation.

daily.q: Which range of adult cycle lengths is generally considered typical?
daily.explain: Twenty-eight days is an average, not a target. What matters more is consistency for you.

daily.q: Which blood test shows low iron stores before anaemia appears?
daily.explain: A full blood count can look normal while ferritin, the storage measure, is already low. Heavy periods deplete iron faster than diet replaces it.

daily.q: When do anti-inflammatories such as ibuprofen work best for period cramps?
options: Once pain is at its peak
daily.explain: They reduce prostaglandin production, so they work considerably better taken early than at peak pain.

daily.q: Roughly how long is the fertile window each cycle?
daily.explain: Sperm can survive up to about five days and an egg under a day, so conception is possible across roughly the five days before ovulation plus the day itself.

daily.q: True or false: a positive ovulation test means an egg will always be released.
daily.explain: A positive test shows an LH surge happened. People with PCOS can have chronically high LH, and some cycles surge without releasing an egg.

daily.q: Why does sleep often get lighter in the week before a period?
options: Core body temperature stays raised and progesterone is falling
daily.explain: Falling asleep depends on core temperature dropping, and it stays raised through the luteal phase.

daily.q: Is exclusive breastfeeding a reliable form of contraception?
options: No, ovulation can return before the first period
daily.explain: It delays ovulation but not reliably, and ovulation returns before the first period, so the first fertile cycle is invisible.

daily.q: Why does cycliq show a predicted window instead of a single day?
options: Calendar math cannot pin the exact day
daily.explain: Calendar predictions can give a reasonable window but not a day, so the window widens when your own cycles vary.

daily.q: Thin grey discharge with a fishy smell usually suggests what?
daily.explain: That is not part of the normal cycle rhythm. It usually means bacterial vaginosis and needs treatment, not tracking.

daily.q: When is a urine pregnancy test reasonably reliable?
options: From the day a period is due
daily.explain: hCG only becomes detectable a few days after implantation. Testing earlier produces false negatives.

hormones.q: Which hormone surge triggers the release of the egg?
hormones.explain: A surge of luteinising hormone triggers ovulation.

hormones.q: Which hormone raises basal body temperature after ovulation?
hormones.explain: Progesterone from the corpus luteum stabilises the lining and raises basal temperature.

phases.q: Which phase absorbs most of the variation between cycles?
phases.explain: The luteal phase is relatively fixed for a person. The follicular phase is what varies.

phases.q: A 34-day cycle is most often explained by:
phases.explain: A long cycle is usually a late ovulation, not a long second half.

variation.q: Which is a reason to talk to a clinician?
options: A cycle three days longer than last month
Periods stopping for three months when not pregnant
variation.explain: Three months without a period, cycles outside 21 to 35 days, or a persistent change of a week or more are the thresholds.

variation.q: Adult cycles of about how many days are considered typical?
variation.explain: The typical adult range is about 21 to 35 days.

symptoms.q: Bloating, tender breasts and disrupted sleep cluster mostly in which phase?
symptoms.explain: These are luteal-phase symptoms, driven by high progesterone.

symptoms.q: Period cramps come from which chemicals making the uterus contract?
symptoms.explain: Prostaglandins make the uterine muscle contract to shed its lining.

tracking.q: Which logging habit makes data most useful?
options: Logging everything, but only on bad days
Logging a small set every day
tracking.explain: A small set logged daily gives a usable baseline. Only logging bad days makes every day look bad.

tracking.q: Why do period start dates need to be accurate?
options: Every prediction is anchored to them
tracking.explain: A start date logged two days late shifts the whole forward projection.

window.q: How long can sperm survive in fertile cervical mucus?
window.explain: Sperm can survive up to about five days in fertile mucus.

window.q: How long does an egg survive after release?
window.explain: An egg survives roughly 12 to 24 hours.

signals.q: Which signal only confirms ovulation after it has happened?
signals.explain: Temperature rises after ovulation, so it confirms rather than predicts.

signals.q: An LH surge comes about how long before ovulation?
signals.explain: That lead time is why a positive LH test is predictive.

frequency.q: Which approach gives close to the maximum chance without needing the exact day?
options: Sex every one to two days across the window
One attempt on the predicted day
frequency.explain: Frequency across the window removes the need to be right about which day it is.

options: Calendars cannot pin down the exact day
frequency.explain: Ovulation timing varies, so aiming at one date risks missing the window.

expectations.q: About what share of couples conceive within a year of regular unprotected sex?
expectations.explain: Roughly 80% within a year and around 90% within two.

expectations.q: For a healthy couple in their late twenties, the chance per cycle is about:
expectations.explain: Several months without success is statistically ordinary.

help.q: Under 35 with no known factors, assessment is usually advised after:
help.explain: Twelve months of trying under age 35.

help.q: At 35 or over, assessment is usually advised after:
help.explain: Six months at 35 or over, and straight away if there are known factors.

options: The first day of the last period
dating.explain: That is why the first two weeks precede conception.

dating.q: What does a first-trimester scan do to the due date?
options: Redates it when it disagrees meaningfully
dating.explain: A first-trimester ultrasound is accurate to within about five days and is used to redate.

first.q: Which supplement is advised daily, ideally from before conception?
first.explain: Folic acid matters most while the neural tube is closing.

second.q: The anatomy scan is around which weeks?
second.explain: It checks growth, placenta and the development of major organs.

second.q: When does glucose screening for gestational diabetes usually happen?

third.q: If your baby's usual movements reduce, you should:
options: Contact your midwife or maternity unit the same day
third.explain: Same day, every time, without waiting and without trying cold drinks or sugar first.
Labour contractions get longer, stronger and closer together regardless of what you do.

warnings.explain: Any bleeding, severe headache, visual changes, sudden swelling or reduced movements.

warnings.q: Your waters break and the fluid is green or bloody. You should:
warnings.explain: Green or bloody fluid needs immediate contact.

pcos-criteria.q: PCOS is usually diagnosed from how many of the three features?
pcos-criteria.explain: Two of three: irregular ovulation, androgen excess, polycystic-appearing ovaries.

pcos-criteria.q: Do follicles seen on a scan alone diagnose PCOS?
pcos-criteria.explain: The follicles are not cysts, and a scan alone does not diagnose the syndrome.

pcos-manage.q: Which is now generally first line for ovulation induction in PCOS?
pcos-manage.explain: Letrozole is generally ahead of clomifene.

pcos-manage.q: Insulin resistance in PCOS is commonly addressed with:
pcos-manage.explain: Movement improves insulin sensitivity, and metformin is the usual medication.

endo-pattern.q: Period pain that starts days before the bleeding is:
options: Part of the pattern that should prompt referral
endo-pattern.explain: It is one of the features worth raising, with pain that limits daily activity.

endo-pattern.q: How well does the extent of endometriosis predict pain?
endo-pattern.explain: Minimal disease can hurt severely and extensive disease can be silent.

advocacy.q: What changes clinical decisions most in a short appointment?
options: Dated symptoms and what you can no longer do
advocacy.explain: Effects change decisions. Adjectives do not.

advocacy.q: If pain is dismissed without examination or a plan:
advocacy.explain: A second opinion is reasonable and normal.

options: Twelve consecutive months without a period
timeline.explain: It is a retrospective point after twelve consecutive months.

options: A persistent cycle-length change of seven days or more
timeline.explain: Late transition brings gaps of 60 days or longer.

symptoms.explain: That is why symptoms come and go unpredictably.

symptoms.q: Periods often get ___ before they get lighter.
symptoms.explain: Heavier bleeding is common early in the transition.

treatment.q: Which is the most effective treatment for hot flashes and night sweats?
treatment.explain: It is the most effective, and it also protects bone density.

treatment.q: If you have a uterus, oestrogen therapy needs:
treatment.explain: The progestogen protects the lining of the uterus.

options: Twelve months after the final period
beyond.explain: Ovulation still happens intermittently during perimenopause.

beyond.q: Which treats vaginal dryness with minimal absorption?
beyond.explain: It is suitable for many people who cannot take systemic therapy.
